$comment: 'One user action produces one request — no amplification.' A budget is raised
only with a recorded justification; the reviewer checklist treats a raised
budget as an architecture change, not a tuning knob.
Recordings are produced by the Playwright run (apps/web/e2e) and compared here.
A budgeted interaction with no recording FAILS: a broken e2e run must not be
able to satisfy the budget by producing nothing.
Every 'maxRequests' below is a MEASURED number, not a target. The measurement
is the recording in ./recordings/, produced by the real browser against the
real production bundle at both viewports.

interactions.description: Cold load of the application shell, to first settled connection state.
interactions.note: Document, JS bundle, CSS bundle, favicon, and the one /api/health call. Headroom is deliberate: this is a page load, not a user action.

interactions.description: User clicks 'Check again' in the connection panel.
interactions.note: I-10 in its strictest form. One click, one request. Any retry, revalidation, or telemetry beat would break this and is meant to.

interactions.description: User clicks 'New rule' to open the rule-authoring form.
interactions.note: I-13, in the same strict form as catalogue-open-new-shift-type. A control labelled New must persist nothing before a completed form and an explicit Save. ZERO is the only correct number and this budget can never be raised without the invariant changing first. Measured 0 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-002).

interactions.description: User clicks 'Save rule' and the server refuses it with a 422.
interactions.note: One Save, one request. A refused save does NOT refetch, because nothing changed. Measured 1 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-002).

interactions.description: User clicks 'Save rule' and the server accepts it.
interactions.note: The write plus ONE invalidation refetch of the rule list. Two is the measured number, not a target: the list must reflect the new rule and the client does not synthesise it from the response. Measured 2 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-002).

interactions.description: User clicks 'New period' to open the period-authoring form.
interactions.note: I-13, in the same strict form as catalogue-open-new-shift-type and rules-open-new-rule. A control labelled New must persist nothing before a completed form and an explicit Save. ZERO is the only correct number and this budget can never be raised without the invariant changing first. Measured 0 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-004).

interactions.description: User fills every field of the period form and does not submit.
interactions.note: The other half of I-13: not only does opening the form write nothing, filling it issues nothing either. A field that fetched or saved on change would put a half-entered planning window on the wire. Measured 0 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-004).

interactions.description: User clicks 'Save period' and the server refuses it with a 422.
interactions.note: One Save, one request. A refused save does NOT refetch, because nothing changed. Measured 1 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-004).

interactions.description: User opens a grid cell to see and edit its assignments.
interactions.note: ZERO, and deliberately so: the cell editor renders from the grid the page already holds rather than re-reading the cell. An earlier design fetched the candidate list on open, which would have made opening a cell cost a request for information the user had not yet asked for; the candidate read moved behind 'Assign someone' instead, which is the budget below. Measured 0 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-004).

interactions.description: User clicks 'Assign someone' inside the cell editor.
interactions.note: I-10 in its strictest form: one action, one read. The candidate list is credential-derived and per (date, shift type), so it cannot come from the grid payload. Measured 1 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-004).

interactions.description: User saves a manual assignment into a cell and the server accepts it.
interactions.note: TWO, under the same ruling as catalogue-save-shift-type: the POST plus the server-authoritative grid re-read. PO-DEC-18 makes the server the authority on what the schedule now says, so after a mutation the client re-reads rather than patching its own cache from the response and rendering a grid no server ever produced. Amplification is N requests for one action's WORK; this is one write plus one read-back. Measured 2 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-004).

interactions.description: User confirms 'New draft' and a draft version is created.
interactions.note: The POST plus the server-authoritative version-list re-read, under the same ruling as catalogue-save-shift-type. Measured 2 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-004, review N-7).

interactions.description: User saves a staffing requirement and the server accepts it.
interactions.note: The PUT plus the requirement-list re-read. The write carries a compare-and-set token, so the re-read is also how the author learns the new token — patching the cache from the response would leave the client holding a revision the server never issued. Measured 2 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-004, review N-7).

interactions.description: User pins or unpins an assignment in the cell editor.
interactions.note: The PUT plus the grid re-read. A pin is a solver INPUT, not a display toggle, so the grid must show what the server stored rather than what the browser assumed. Measured 2 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-004, review N-7).

interactions.description: User removes an assignment, giving a reason.
interactions.note: The POST plus the grid re-read. Measured 2 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-004, review N-7).

interactions.description: User clicks 'Edit' on an existing rule to open it in the form.
interactions.note: ZERO: the form is filled from the rule list the page already holds. A fetch here would be amplification of a control that only opens a form, and it would also make the edit round trip depend on a second read that could disagree with the row the user clicked. Measured 0 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-004, review N-7).

interactions.description: User saves changes to an existing rule.
interactions.note: The PUT plus the rule-list re-read. Measured 2 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-004, review N-7).

interactions.description: User clicks 'New shift type' to open the authoring form.
interactions.note: I-13, and the reason the invariant exists: a control labelled New must persist nothing before a completed form and an explicit Save. ZERO is the only correct number here — this budget can never be raised without the invariant changing first. Measured 0 at both viewports.

interactions.description: User clicks Save and the server refuses the shift type with a 422.
interactions.note: One Save, one request. A refused save does NOT refetch, because nothing changed and there is nothing new to fetch — which is what makes the two-request success budget below a property of the success path rather than of Save in general. Measured 1 at both viewports.

interactions.description: User fills every field on the activation form and does not submit.
interactions.note: I-13, on a credential-setting form. ZERO is the only correct number: a field that saved on change would put a half-typed password on the wire, and an activation form that wrote on mount would consume an invitation token nobody submitted. This budget can never be raised without the invariant changing first. Measured 0 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-001).

interactions.description: User submits an empty activation form; the CLIENT refuses it.
interactions.note: A client-side pre-check that still called the server would be the amplification I-10 forbids, dressed as helpfulness. Measured 0 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-001).

interactions.description: User submits the password-reset request form.
interactions.note: I-10 in its strictest form: one submit, one POST. There is no read-back, because the response is deliberately identical whatever the server found — there is nothing to re-read. Measured 1 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-001).

interactions.description: User clicks Save and the server accepts the shift type (200).
interactions.note: TWO, ruled and justified — not an I-10 exception. The POST plus the server-authoritative list refetch is the PO-DEC-18 display posture: after a mutation the client re-reads what the SERVER says the list is, rather than patching its own cache from the response and rendering a view no server ever produced. The second request is therefore the invariant's intent (one action, one authoritative round trip to re-establish truth) rather than amplification of it — amplification is N requests for one action's WORK, and this is one write plus one read-back. A one-request alternative exists (POST returns the row; the client updates the list from it) and is recorded as a later-packet option; it is deliberately NOT implemented, because it moves the rendered list's authority to the client. Ruled by Fable on the OPUS-M2-004 escalation (packet 30 §6a as amended). Measured 2 at both viewports: POST .../catalogue/shift-types, then GET .../catalogue/shift-types.

interactions.description: User clicks 'Add a location' to open the authoring form.
interactions.note: I-13, in the same strict form as catalogue-open-new-shift-type and rules-open-new-rule. A control labelled Add must persist nothing before a completed form, validation, and an explicit Save. ZERO is the only correct number and this budget can never be raised without the invariant changing first. Measured 0 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-007).

interactions.description: User clicks Save and the server accepts the location (200).
interactions.note: The POST plus ONE server-authoritative list refetch, under the same PO-DEC-18 ruling the catalogue's accepted-save budget carries: after a mutation the client re-reads what the SERVER says the list is rather than patching its own cache and rendering a view no server produced. One write plus one read-back is not amplification. Measured 2 at both viewports: POST .../settings/locations, then GET .../settings/locations (OPUS-M3-007).

interactions.description: User acknowledges the published-schedule impact and saves a new group time zone (204).
interactions.note: The PUT plus ONE re-read of the settings, same ruling as above — and here the read-back is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: the settings response carries the optimistic-concurrency token (groups.settings_version) that the next save must echo, so a client that patched its own cache would save against a version it invented. Measured 2 at both viewports: PUT .../settings/timezone, then GET .../settings (OPUS-M3-007).

interactions.description: User saves a time-zone change without acknowledging the published-schedule impact; the server refuses it with a 422.
interactions.note: One Save, one request. A refused save does NOT refetch, because nothing changed and there is nothing new to read — which is what makes the two-request success budget above a property of the success path rather than of Save in general. Measured 1 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-007).

interactions.description: User clicks 'Publish this version…' to open the confirmation panel.
interactions.note: I-13, on an act that is not a create but is irreversible: publication cannot be undone, only superseded, so nothing may reach the server before an explicit confirmation. ZERO is the only correct number and this budget can never be raised without the invariant changing first. Measured 0 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-005).

interactions.description: User ticks the acknowledgement and types the confirmation phrase, and does not submit.
interactions.note: The other half of I-13: filling the confirmation issues nothing. A field that validated on the server per keystroke would also breach I-10. Measured 0 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-005).

interactions.description: User confirms a publication and the server accepts it.
interactions.note: The POST plus ONE server-authoritative re-read of the review, under the PO-DEC-18 ruling the catalogue's accepted-save budget carries: after a mutation the client re-reads what the SERVER says rather than patching its own cache. The read-back is load-bearing here rather than cosmetic — the re-read carries the new blockers (the version is now published) and the new compare-and-set token. Measured 2 at both viewports: POST .../versions/:id/publication, then GET .../versions/:id/publication-review (OPUS-M3-005).

interactions.description: User confirms a publication and the server refuses it with a 422.
interactions.note: One confirmation, one request. A refused publication does NOT refetch, because nothing changed — which is what makes the two-request success budget a property of the success path rather than of the confirm control in general. Measured 1 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-005).

interactions.description: User clicks 'Clone into a new draft…' on a published version.
interactions.note: I-13 in its literal form: a control that creates a draft must persist nothing before an explicit confirm. ZERO is the only correct number and this budget can never be raised without the invariant changing first. Measured 0 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-005).

interactions.description: User clicks 'Revert to this version…' on a superseded version.
interactions.note: A revert publishes forward and changes the live schedule, so it earns the same treatment as publication: the control opens a typed confirmation and issues nothing. Measured 0 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-005).

interactions.description: User changes 'Compare against' on the version-comparison screen.
interactions.note: TWO GETs, and both are load-bearing rather than amplification: the change-level comparison and the person-level affected-staff set are separate reads by design. The affected set is what a notification fan-out would use, so "who would be told about this?" has to be answerable on its own rather than depending on a client having fetched the whole change list first — the same reasoning the two endpoints were split under (VersionComparisonPage's docblock). One user action, one authoritative round trip per view, no third request and no re-read of the history the page already holds. Added on review finding N1: the interaction existed with no budget entry, so no gate held the count. Measured 2 at both viewports (OPUS-M3-005).
